description: Golden OIB retrieval set for broad/exact/paraphrased German queries (backlog item 12). File-level labels: each entry names the corpus FILES that answer it (real data/oib filenames, verified against the checkout — never invented). Cohorts: (a) overview — broad 'was weißt du über ...' questions with no usable lexical signal (the item-11 failure class); (b) exact-id — §-refs, RL designations, filenames; (c) paraphrase — the same intents in everyday wording. calibration_pending is true on every entry: file membership was read from the corpus layout, not yet reviewed by a second building-law reader.

entries.question: was weißt du über die oib 2
entries.notes: The item-11 exemplar, verbatim lowercase as users type it. Lowercase 'oib' yields zero exact terms (legal_terms.isupper) and the sparse survivors die at the DF ceiling / digit-only rule, so current retrieval reaches only the vector channel.

entries.question: § 5.1.1 OIB-RL 2 Gehweglänge
entries.notes: Punkt 5.1.1 verified in fixtures/punkt_index.json (RL 2). The OIB uses 'Punkt', not '§' — users write § anyway (item 11). The § half matches no chunk text; the OIB-RL half must carry the recall.

entries.notes: Punkt 2.4.1 verified in fixtures/punkt_index.json (RL 4). Same loose-§ shape as ex-paragraph-rl2.

entries.notes: Punkt 3 verified in fixtures/punkt_index.json (RL 6). Bare §-ref with no content noun.

entries.question: OIB-RL 2
entries.notes: Uppercase designation. Yields the ALLCAPS exact term 'OIB-RL' — the case asymmetry against ov-rl2 ('oib 2' yields nothing) is the item-13 axis.

entries.question: OIB-Richtlinie 4
entries.notes: Full-spelling designation. Yields the exact term 'OIB-Richtlinie 4' (case-insensitive name token + number).

entries.question: OIB-RL 2.1
entries.notes: Sub-Richtlinie designation. Exact term 'OIB-RL'; the '2.1' number is lexical signal only if it survives selection (dotted numbers are not digit-only).

entries.question: Leitfaden zur OIB-Richtlinie 6
entries.notes: Leitfaden request. Exact term 'OIB-Richtlinie 6'; 'Leitfaden' must separate the guide from the Richtlinie itself via the sparse channel.

entries.question: oib-rl_2_ausgabe_mai_2023.pdf
entries.notes: Literal filename as typed. Lowercase, so no exact term fires; the sparse channel sees only corpus-identity lexemes ('oib', 'ausgabe') and digits. Only the vector channel (filename is embedded text) can serve this in production — the deterministic channels honestly score ~0.
